name: protrusion_enclosure_membrane
description: Active-protrusion membrane-wrapping mechanics (eukaryogenesis S3, continuum energetics). Tests whether an actin-driven host protrusion supplies enough work to carry a lipid membrane over the Helfrich bending barrier to a stable fully wrapped state around a bacterial partner, given adhesion, membrane tension, and a finite protrusion-area reservoir. Emits enclosure PROBABILITY over a partner-radius ensemble and the share of enclosures that require the active force — the mechanism the question is about, not passive differential adhesion. Validated against the classic wrapping threshold (reduced adhesion = 2). The next fidelity rung is a triangulated-mesh run (pbg-mem3dg).

max_membrane_area_um2.description: membrane area the protrusion can deploy

wrap.doc:
Active-protrusion membrane-wrapping transition (eukaryogenesis S3, continuum
energetics). Over a partner-radius ensemble it emits the enclosure PROBABILITY
(fraction that reach a stable full wrap), the wrapping size window, and the
share of enclosures that NEED the active protrusion (adhesion alone would not
cross the barrier) — so the active mechanism is explicit, not assumed.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
